wording: description: "German trade tax (Gewerbesteuer, GewSt) for collection period 2026: who is liable (sole traders and partnerships with a commercial business, every GmbH, UG and AG; free professions excluded), trade income (Gewerbeertrag) with the § 8 add-backs (one quarter of financing items above EUR 200,000) and § 9 reductions (Grundsteuer, partnership shares, 15% participation exemption, donations), the EUR 24,500 allowance, the 3.5% base rate, the municipal multiplier (Hebesatz, at least 200% for 2026, 280% from 2027), the § 35 EStG income tax credit (four times the base amount, capped), loss carry-forward (EUR 1 million plus 60%), apportionment between municipalities (Zerlegung), the return, quarterly prepayments, surcharges and interest. Trigger on: Gewerbesteuer, GewSt, Hebesatz, Gewerbeertrag, Steuermessbetrag, Freibetrag 24.500, Hinzurechnungen, Kürzungen, § 35 EStG, Zerlegung, Gewerbesteuer-Vorauszahlung, trade tax Germany. Out of scope: income tax of the owner (de-self-employed-income-tax, de-income-tax), partners' income (de-partners-and-part-year), corporate income tax (de-corporate-tax), non-residents (de-non-resident-tax)."

wording: Collection period (Erhebungszeitraum) 2026 is the calendar year 2026 ([§ 14 GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__14.html)). Trade tax is a municipal tax with two authorities. The tax office sets the base amount in the Gewerbesteuermessbescheid, and that notice also decides whether the business is liable at all ([§ 184(1) AO](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ao_1977/__184.html)). The municipality applies its multiplier, issues the trade tax notice and collects the tax ([§ 16(1) GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__16.html)).

wording: **1. Start from the profit.** Trade income (Gewerbeertrag) is the profit under income tax or corporation tax rules for the matching year, plus § 8 add-backs, minus § 9 reductions ([§ 7 GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__7.html)). Trade tax is not a business expense, so the profit is before trade tax ([§ 4(5b) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__4.html)). For a partnership the profit includes partners' pay for work, loans and assets let to it ([§ 15(1) no. 2 EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__15.html)). Gains on selling a partnership business or share count, unless they fall to a natural person who is a direct partner (§ 7 sentence 2). A business with HGB books and a different financial year counts the profit in the period in which the financial year ends ([§ 10(2) GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__10.html)). If liability does not last the whole year, the period is shortened ([§ 14 GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__14.html)); § 11 does not cut the allowance for a short period.
disposition: Exact predecessor current unit, native coordinates rebound

wording: **4. Deduct trade losses ([§ 10a GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__10a.html)).** Losses of earlier periods reduce trade income in full up to EUR 1 million, and above that up to 60% of the excess. The rest carries forward. There is no carry-back, and § 10d EStG does not apply. The loss left at the end of each period is determined separately. In a partnership, losses and the EUR 1 million are split by the general profit-sharing key, without advance shares. A new owner cannot use the losses of a business taken over as a whole (§ 10a sentence 8). For companies, § 8c and § 8d KStG apply; refer changes of partners or shareholders. The Federal Constitutional Court held sentences 1 and 2 compatible with the Basic Law (decision of 23 July 2025, 2 BvL 19/14, noted on the statute page).

wording:
**6. Apportion between municipalities (Zerlegung).** If the business had permanent establishments in more than one municipality during the period, or one establishment spans two, or it moved, the tax office splits the base amount ([§ 28(1) GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__28.html)). The key uses the qualifying statutory wages of each establishment under § 31, then rounds them down to full EUR 1,000 ([§ 29 GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__29.html)). Where the business is not run by a legal person, EUR 25,000 a year in total is added as wages for the working owners ([§ 31(5) GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__31.html)). Wind, solar and storage businesses use installed capacity for nine tenths (§ 29(1) no. 2 and 3). Each municipality then applies its own multiplier to its share ([§ 4(1) GewStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gewstg/__4.html)).

**Qualifying apportionment wages (§ 31(1)–(4) GewStG).** Start with employment remuneration under § 19(1) no. 1 EStG, excluding amounts exempt from income tax under other legislation. Include overtime and Sunday, public-holiday and night-work supplements regardless of their income-tax treatment. Exclude remuneration paid to people employed for vocational training and one-off remuneration calculated by profit. For each individual employee, exclude the remaining remuneration above EUR 50,000. Where the business is partly trade-tax exempt, exclude pay of employees who do not work exclusively or predominantly in the taxable business or part. Apply these employee rules before aggregating the establishment's qualifying wages and applying the § 29 rounding and apportionment key. The separate total EUR 25,000 working-owner amount under § 31(5) remains as stated above.

For a stipulated ordinary corporation with two establishments, one employee at A paid EUR 100,000 and one at B paid EUR 50,000, with no trainee pay, profit-based bonus or other adjustment, qualifying wages are EUR 50,000 at each establishment. A EUR 1,000 base amount therefore splits EUR 500 to each, before each municipality applies its own multiplier. The uncapped 2:1 salary ratio is not the statutory key.
disposition: Bounded source/condition successor

The separate overrides remain: a business with a loss carry-forward determined at the end of the last period; any business the tax office asks. A sole trader at or below EUR 24,500 with no loss carry-forward and no request files nothing. Note the test is on trade income before rounding: EUR 24,580 rounds to EUR 24,500, gives no tax, yet a return is due.

wording:
**Example 1: sole trader in Munich, ordinary costs.** A trader runs a shop in Munich. Profit before trade tax EUR 80,000. Loan interest EUR 12,000 (in full), shop rent EUR 36,000 (one half, EUR 18,000), leasing of a petrol car EUR 10,000 (one fifth, EUR 2,000). The financing sum is EUR 32,000, not above EUR 200,000, so nothing is added back. No § 9 reductions. Trade income EUR 80,000 is already a full EUR 100. Less the allowance of EUR 24,500 leaves EUR 55,500. Times 3.5% gives a base amount of EUR 1,942.50. Munich's multiplier of 490% gives trade tax of EUR 9,518.25. The § 35 credit is four times the base amount, EUR 7,770, which is below the trade tax; assuming the income tax on the commercial income is at least that, the credit is EUR 7,770 and EUR 1,748.25 of trade tax stays a cost. Next year's prepayments are one quarter of EUR 9,518.25, rounded down: EUR 2,379 on each date.

```oa-check
name: Sole trader in Munich, profit EUR 80,000 (2026)
inputs:
  profit: 80000
  interest: 12000
  shop_rent: 36000
  car_lease: 10000
  allowance: 24500
  multiplier: 490
steps:
  - financing_sum: interest + shop_rent / 2 + car_lease / 5
  - add_back: max(financing_sum - 200000, 0) / 4
  - trade_income: profit + add_back
  - rounded: floor(trade_income / 100) * 100
  - taxable: max(rounded - allowance, 0)
  - base_amount: taxable * 0.035
  - trade_tax: base_amount * multiplier / 100
  - credit: min(4 * base_amount, trade_tax)
  - not_offset: trade_tax - credit
  - prepayment: floor(trade_tax / 4)
expected:
  financing_sum: 32000
  add_back: 0
  base_amount: 1942.50
  trade_tax: 9518.25
  credit: 7770.00
  not_offset: 1748.25
  prepayment: 2379
```

wording:
**Example 2: partnership above the add-back allowance, with a property and old losses.** A KG (two equal partners) has profit of EUR 1,400,000. It paid interest of EUR 180,000 (in full) and warehouse rent of EUR 120,000 (one half, EUR 60,000): sum EUR 240,000, excess over EUR 200,000 is EUR 40,000, one quarter, EUR 10,000, is added. It owns its office building and booked Grundsteuer of EUR 6,000, which is deducted. Trade income before losses is EUR 1,404,000. Losses brought forward are EUR 2,000,000. It deducts EUR 1,000,000 in full plus 60% of the EUR 404,000 above it (EUR 242,400): EUR 1,242,400 in all. Trade income left is EUR 161,600; EUR 757,600 of loss carries forward. Less the EUR 24,500 allowance leaves EUR 137,100, and 3.5% gives a base amount of EUR 4,798.50. Assume the municipality's multiplier is 410% (the 2025 national average): trade tax EUR 19,673.85. Each partner's 50% share of the base amount is EUR 2,399.25, so each partner's § 35 credit is capped first at EUR 9,597 (four times the share), which is below the partner's half of the tax payable.

```oa-check
name: KG with add-back, Grundsteuer and loss carry-forward (2026)
inputs:
  profit: 1400000
  interest: 180000
  warehouse_rent: 120000
  grundsteuer: 6000
  losses_bf: 2000000
  allowance: 24500
  multiplier: 410
  partner_share: 0.5
steps:
  - financing_sum: interest + warehouse_rent / 2
  - add_back: max(financing_sum - 200000, 0) / 4
  - before_losses: profit + add_back - grundsteuer
  - loss_limit: min(before_losses, 1000000) + max(before_losses - 1000000, 0) * 0.6
  - loss_used: min(losses_bf, loss_limit)
  - trade_income: before_losses - loss_used
  - loss_cf: losses_bf - loss_used
  - rounded: floor(trade_income / 100) * 100
  - base_amount: max(rounded - allowance, 0) * 0.035
  - trade_tax: base_amount * multiplier / 100
  - partner_credit_cap: 4 * base_amount * partner_share
expected:
  add_back: 10000
  before_losses: 1404000
  loss_used: 1242400
  loss_cf: 757600
  base_amount: 4798.50
  trade_tax: 19673.85
  partner_credit_cap: 9597.00
```

wording:
- What exactly does the business do, and is it run alone, in a partnership or through a company? Does any part involve selling goods or reselling others' products? (Decides liability.) For a partnership, can its own commercial and noncommercial activities be separated, what are each activity's and total annual net receipts, and is any commercial income instead from another partnership?
- In which municipalities did it have premises in 2026, and did it move? Which multiplier is on the last trade tax notice? (Decides the multiplier and any apportionment.) For apportionment, obtain pay by employee and establishment, trainee status, profit-based one-off bonuses, tax-exempt items and overtime/Sunday/holiday/night supplements, so the per-employee EUR 50,000 limit and § 31 exclusions can be applied.
- What did it pay in the year for interest, annuities, silent partners, rent and leasing (movable and immovable separately) and licences? (Decides the § 8 add-back.)
- Does it own real property with Grundsteuer booked as an expense, hold shares in partnerships or companies (and what percentage at 1 January), or make donations? (Decides § 9.)
- Was a trade loss carry-forward determined at the end of 2025? (Decides § 10a and the return duty.)
- Is a Steuerberater preparing the return, and what other income does the owner have? (Decides the deadline and the § 35 cap.)

wording: **Separable own commercial side activity: annual net-receipt test.** Under the BFH interpretation adopted in BMF EStH 2025 H 15.8(5), an otherwise noncommercial partnership's separable own commercial activity does not reclassify the rest if BOTH `commercial net receipts ≤ 0.03 × total partnership net receipts` AND `commercial net receipts ≤ EUR 24,500` for the assessment period. Total receipts include the commercial and noncommercial activities, excluding VAT. Apply the same test whether the commercial branch makes a profit or a loss. The branch remains commercial in its own right; an inseparably commercial overall activity does not become a free profession under this exception. This own-activity test does not apply to commercial income received through a participation in another partnership; keep that income-tax limb and its separate trade-tax treatment distinct.

wording: For an otherwise qualifying separable professional partnership, total net receipts of EUR 500,000 and commercial net receipts of EUR 15,000 pass both gates exactly; EUR 15,000.01 fails the 3% gate. At total net receipts of EUR 1,000,000, commercial receipts of EUR 24,500 pass both; EUR 24,500.01 fails the absolute gate although below 3%. These are receipts tests, not a profit allowance. The outcome under these two gates is unchanged if the commercial branch has a loss.
